verdict.probe_answer: Arm A: the main recovery/fail-open/free-fn tests should fail on the pre-change branch, and most assert real behavior with pool-size guards plus concrete target/confidence checks. Strongest test: scope_graph_free_fn_path_not_misrouted_to_colliding_method_pool, because it pins the colliding method bucket and asserts the resolved file is the module free function. Weakest test: scope_graph_macro_wildcard_shadow_keeps_all, because it does not assert a non-empty or >=2 result, so the confidence check could be vacuous if an empty hit were returned. Arm A also misses the required mixed-edition keep-all fixture. Arm B: same core tests should fail on pre-change, and it adds the mixed-edition keep-all case, so coverage is closer to the brief. Strongest test: scope_graph_free_fn_path_not_misrouted_to_colliding_method_pool, for the same concrete misroute assertion; the mixed-edition test is also valuable because it exercises a separate fail-open edge. Weakest test: scope_graph_macro_wildcard_shadow_keeps_all, for the same vacuous all() risk.
verdict.rationale: Both arms implement the same narrowly scoped resolution integration: free-function guard, owner-method prune via ScopeResolution, and fail-open only through owner_lookup_in_modules. I do not see an implementation difference that makes one code path materially safer. The material difference is test completeness. WRONG: Arm A omits the task-required mixed-edition keep-all fixture, so it is not complete against the stated integration test list. SMELL: both arms' macro wildcard test should assert the retained pool size, not only all confidences. Arm B covers the mixed-edition negative path and stays within the requested files, making it materially better overall.
